newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF says not heard BOJ mulling policy change.
newsitem.headline: MOF says not heard BOJ mulling policy change.

text.p: A Ministry of Finance (MOF) official said on Friday that the ministry has heard nothing to indicate that the Bank of Japan (BOJ) may be considering a change in monetary policy.

There was market talk that the BOJ may raise interest rates to prevent more financial institutions having difficulties due to low returns from investment amid a negative interest rate spread resulting from Japan's low interest rates.

"We are not aware that the Bank of Japan is considering a change in its monetary policy related to an order this morning calling on Nissan Mutual Life Insurance Co to halt some of its operations," the MOF official said.
A BOJ spokesman declined to comment on the market talk.
"We do not make any comments on each such rumour," said the spokesman.
Separately, BOJ Governor Yasuo Matsushita told a parliamentary committee on Friday morning that the BOJ intended to maintain its current monetary policy.
Matsushita said the easy money policy, along with other past policies, had led to solid capital spending in Japan.
"We will maintain the current monetary policy, so that we'll be able to conclude that the recovery has become certain," he said.
Earlier on Friday, the MOF had ordered Nissan Mutual Life Insurance Co to halt some of its operations.

Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told a regular news conference that the ministry had received a report from Nissan Life that it had come to a decision to discontinue business at an emergency board meeting held earlier on Friday.
Mitsuzuka said Nissan Life's failure was due to its failed asset management, but added that there would be no similar cases at other life insurance companies.
